title: Subcontractor Margin Chain
summary: Protect agency job margins by linking client commitments, subcontractor costs, approvals, and invoices.
user: Boutique agencies that deliver through freelancers and subcontractors but need to see end-client commitments, subcontractor cost, approval, and invoice status in one job chain. Paying customer: agency owner; wedge: job-level margin protection at $79/month.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The author reports interviews with 60+ freelancers, creators, and small agencies who lose 20–30% of time and revenue to work split across Gmail/WhatsApp, Notion, payment links, and spreadsheets.
A feature request asks for end-client/sub-client relationships across clients, projects, tasks, and invoices for subcontracted work.

recurrence: Both qualitative agency interviews and an invoicing feature request point to the same missing link between the buyer, delivery partner, work, and cash.
current_workaround: Create separate client/project records, keep subcontractor rates in spreadsheets, and reconcile profitability only after invoices are paid.
incumbents_and_gap: Harvest, Bonsai, HoneyBook, and Invoice Ninja cover pieces of time, invoices, or portals. They do not make a nested end-client-to-subcontractor margin chain the core operational record.
smallest_useful_product: A job chain with end client, agency client, subcontractors, approved scope, committed cost, invoice milestones, and margin-at-risk alerts. Non-goals: payroll, marketplace hiring, general project management, or accounting.
success_measure: Pilot agencies record 95% of subcontracted jobs before work starts and catch at least one margin-at-risk job per quarter before invoicing.
monetization: subscription — $79/month per agency is justified by protecting one project's margin and scales by active job chains, not seats.
constraints: Protect contractor rates and client identities with role-based access; do not calculate payroll tax or make employment classifications.
why_distinct: The central object is a commercial delivery chain, not a generic task board or freelancer marketplace.
